content:
alex: Heads up — seeing sustained inference tail latency spikes in us-east-1. Alerts show GPU power-limit events + thermal throttle on several nodes.
ops-bot: Alert: cluster-us-east1-gpupool high_token_latency (p95 > 350ms) — triggered 1772344998 — related metrics: gpu_power_limit, gpu_throttle_count
alex: quick snapshot from monitoring:
```
  node: gpu-node-34a
  gpu0_temp: 94C
  gpu0_power_draw: 270W
  gpu0_power_limit: 250W
  gpu0_throttle: true
  errors: [Xid 62, ECC corrected 1]
```
julian: Xid 62 recurring. That usually points at PCI/thermal stress. Did anyone push firmware or change power capping yesterday?
maria: I rolled a kernel security patch to the fleet at ~02:30 UTC but it was only on control-plane nodes, not compute. No BIOS flasher.
sre-oncall: @alex can you confirm which instance types? we should drain affected nodes before they start failing requests.
alex: These are p4d-like baremetal racks (48xx series). Affected about 6 machines across two racks: gpu-node-34a, gpu-node-34b, gpu-node-57c, gpu-node-81d, gpu-node-81e, gpu-node-81f.
karla: Paging infra-bot for recent power-config changes. Also check iLO/IDRAC logs for sudden power limits.
infra-bot: iDRAC log snippet for gpu-node-81d: 
```
  2026-03-18T01:10:12Z - Thermal trip event, CPU throttled
  2026-03-18T01:10:14Z - Power cap enforced by PSU: 250W (requested 300W)
  2026-03-18T01:10:16Z - Fan 2 error: speed dropped to 0 rpm
```
julian: Fan 2 down -> PSU pulled power -> GPUs hit PL1 cap -> driver reports throttle and Xid 62. That lines up. Could be failing fan or a PSU misreport.
maria: On affected hosts, nvml shows this:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d POWER,TEMPERATURE,DRIVER
GPU 0:
    Power Readings
        Power Draw : 268.12 W
        Power Limit : 250.00 W
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp : 93 C
    Fan Speed : 0 %
    Xid Errors : 62
```
alex: Oof. Fan at 0% consistently. We need to triage quickly — inference gets CPU fallback and latency jumps.
sre-oncall: Plan: 1) immediate soft-drain affected nodes (move active containers off), 2) attach to serial/ILO, power-cycle PSU if fans don't spin up, 3) tag for replace if hardware faults persist. I'll start drain.
ops-bot: Command executed: `fleetctl drain gpu-node-34a,gpu-node-34b,gpu-node-57c,gpu-node-81d,gpu-node-81e,gpu-node-81f --reason "thermal/power throttle"`
karla: Also check our power-management profile — last week infra team changed OEM default from auto to aggressive PL enforcement in an attempt to save 10% electricity. Could be a regression with new PSU firmware.
julian: Can someone pull the dmesg/driver log around the Xid events? Need to confirm whether ECC corrected errors are increasing.
alex: Pasting kernel logs from gpu-node-34a around the event: 
```
[Mar18 01:10:05] nvidia: Xid (62) on GPU 00000000:03:00.0: Reset required
[Mar18 01:10:06] nv_peer_mem: ECC corrected error count: 1
[Mar18 01:10:07] thermal: cooling_device: GPU0: trip limit exceeded
[Mar18 01:10:12] kernel: pcie slot power limit changed by system
```
maria: If Xids require reset, a quick software reset might clear it, but repeated Xids + fans at 0% indicate hardware. Replacing fans/PSU or sending to gate for repair.
sre-oncall: I've kicked a rolling routing tweak to move inference traffic away from us-east-1 GPU pool to dedicated spare capacity in us-west-2 for the next 30m. `routingctl shift --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --weight 0.35`
ops-bot: Routing change applied: partial spillover to us-west-2 successful.
karla: For replacement cadence: if fan fails to spin after remote power-cycling, we mark for 'replace-on-fail' and schedule tech team next-day swap. Also tag hardware under warranty for RMA.
julian: Quick check — is this correlated with burst workload at 00:55 UTC? Could be sustained high token rates pushing cards into prolonged high-power state.
alex: Yes, a customer burst + a batch job coincided. We should add a scheduler cap to prevent long sustained peak for these racks while we triage.
maria: Suggestion: add temporary soft cap on batch jobs targeting p4d racks: `batchctl set-limit --rack p4d-81 --cpu 0.6 --gpu 0.7`
sre-oncall: Done. Also adding an alert rule to escalate if fan_speed == 0 && temp > 85C for >60s.
infra-bot: New alert rule created: thermal_fan_dead_high_temp_us-east1 — threshold 60s — notify #eng-infra + #oncall.
julian: Follow-up ops: capture SMART from PSUs and fans, and a short thermal profile after reboot. If it's reproducible we should blacklist the node from allocation.
karla: I'll open an RMA ticket with vendor with logs attached. Keep the drained nodes offline until hardware swap confirmed.
alex: Thanks all. Quick wins: drained nodes, routing spillover, batch caps, alerting. Next: confirm hardware replacement timeline and postmortem if we see any regrets about routing. :thumbsup:
